main_text.p: & liberalis obsequij infinita erat neglecta Au-thoritas. In facilioribus siquidem minusque, onerosis (ut optimè addit Bernardus) eò contemptus est, damnabilior, quò actus videtur laudabilior. Et annon hocipsum Sauli inculcat Samuel, in sequenti capite, qui cùm missus esset, ut Amalek deleret, regem & nonnulla servasset spolia? Nunquid vult Dominus (inquit) Holocausta aut victimas, & non potiùs ut obediatur voci Domini? Melior est enim obedientia, quàm victima, & auscultare magis, quàm adferre adipem Arietum. Rationem reddit 1.Sam. 15.Gregorius, Moral.l.35.quia per victimas aliena caro, per obedientiam propria voluntas mactatur.

9. Sed ista, vt satis nota, missa facio. Obe-dientiam & Abstinentiam facilè admittunt om-nes, sed quæritur in quibus obediendum sit & abstinendum, & quousq;. Neq; enim vel parentibus, vel cujuscunq; sortis aut conditionis Superioribus in omnibus esse obtemperandum docent Scholastici, & cæca Monachorum obedientia, quâ homines in Bestias aut stipites sic degenerant, vt tanquam cadaver aut senis baculum (sicut præcipiunt Iesuitæ) quo-quo versus se ferri sinant, Christiane libertati Inst. p.3. c.3. [?]

page.notes: The bottom of the scan is cut off, so the text may continue beyond "libertati". The small marks at the foot are not legible and are not transcribed. The marginal note reads "Inst. p.3. c.3." as far as it can be made out; the abbreviation is uncertain. The faint marks in the right margin are show-through and are not transcribed.
